context: The stack is on the left, with its top above its bottom. The vertical array on the right has its first element at the bottom and its last element at the top. Between them, a left-pointing arrow is labeled “Array implementation / Stack interface.”
description: The array’s first-to-last order matches the stack’s bottom-to-top order. Read both from the bottom up in this figure. The gray dashed cells and ellipsis above the last element are labeled “Unused array slots.”

frames.announcement: The array starts with four active elements, [1, 3, 2, 5]. The last element, 5, is the top of the stack.
frames.explanation: The array starts with four active elements, [1, 3, 2, 5] from first to last. The stack has the same order from bottom to top. The first element, 1, is the bottom, and the last element, 5, is the top. Two gray dashed empty slots and an ellipsis appear above 5.
frames.key_state: The initial active array elements are [1, 3, 2, 5] from first to last. The first element, 1, is the bottom of the stack. The last element, 5, is the top, with unused slots above it.
frames.title: Initial stack: the last array element, 5, is on top

frames.announcement: The call push(4) writes 4 in the empty slot at the end of the array. The last element and the top of the stack are now 4.
frames.explanation: The call push(4) is labeled “Add element 4 to the end of the array” on the right. The teal 4 goes into the first empty slot above the old last element, 5. The last-element marker moves up to 4. The array now has five active elements, [1, 3, 2, 5, 4] from first to last, matching the stack from bottom to top. The first element and stack bottom are still 1. The last element and stack top are now 4, with empty space still above.
frames.key_state: After push(4), the active array elements are [1, 3, 2, 5, 4] from first to last. The last element and the top of the stack are now 4.
frames.title: Push 4 at the end of the array

frames.announcement: The call pop() removes and returns the last array element, 4. The last element and the top of the stack are back to 5.
frames.explanation: The call pop() is labeled “Remove the last array element” on the right. It removes and returns the last element, 4. The slot that held 4 again has a gray dashed outline, and the last-element marker moves down to 5. The array is back to four active elements, [1, 3, 2, 5] from first to last, matching the stack from bottom to top. The first element and stack bottom are 1. The last element and stack top are 5.
frames.key_state: After pop() removes and returns the last element, 4, the active array elements are [1, 3, 2, 5] from first to last. The last element and the top of the stack are back to 5.
frames.title: Pop 4 from the end of the array

result: In an array-based stack, a push appends an element to the end of the array and a pop removes the last element. When the array does not need to grow, both take O(1) time and the existing elements stay in place.
summary: The end of the array serves as the top of the stack. Both pushes and pops take place at that end.
title: Pushing and popping with an array
